scenes.text: A crop of new 3D and building tools say an agent can drive them. Which of them can do anything with a scan?
scenes.say: New 3D and building tools say an agent can drive them. Which of them can do anything with a scan?

scenes.headline: How agents edit a shared building model
scenes.sub: Three tools on the road from a scan to an IFC file
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Figaro! I read the code of eight of these tools. Let's place them on the road from capture to model, and open the best one up.

scenes.title: Where a scan goes
scenes.sub: Five stops between the site and the model
scenes.say: Chapter one. Where a scan goes.

scenes.title: From a capture to a building model
scenes.say: A scan to building job has five stops.

items.say: First you capture the site, with a scanner, a three sixty camera or a phone.
Then you build a dense point cloud, or a mesh, or a splat.
items.term: Dense cloud: points from every image pair

items.say: Then walls, slabs and openings get traced over that reference. This is the thin step for every tool here.
Then they become a building model, with types and parameters, written out as an IFC file.
Last, you ship it to a viewer, a client or a renderer. Most of these tools crowd the last two stops.

steps.say: The one working loop from capture to model is not a product. A creator filmed a shrine with a three sixty camera, built a dense point cloud, and handed it to Claude in Blender.
Measured points for position, the images for meaning. On an earlier street scene, a splat from the same kind of data had too many floaters, so the recipe dropped it.

scenes.title: A kernel that holds records
scenes.sub: MutinyBIM keeps every trade in an add-on
scenes.say: Chapter two. A kernel that holds records.

scenes.text: Keep the kernel to records and commits, put each trade in an add-on, and make every edit a command the server runs again and may refuse.
scenes.term: Kernel: the core every add-on builds on
scenes.say: Mutiny BIM is the most serious of the set. Its core keeps records and commits, each trade is an add-on, and every edit is a command the server runs again.

scenes.title: Where a parameter's value comes from
scenes.text: value = own value, else the type's value

parts.say: A parameter is just a key with a unit. If the element sets it, that value wins.
If not, the value comes from the element's type. Clear the override, and the type's value comes back.

scenes.title: A trade arrives as a pack

steps.say: A trade is a pack: a manifest, plus contributions to versioned extension points on one contract.
steps.term: Pack: an add-on in the code

steps.say: Inside, the example pack adds a class for a retention vault, and a parameter for its required volume.
And a lint rule that flags an undersized vault, and a calculation that sizes it.
The model pins the pack's exact version, and IFC export reads the registries, so the new parameter exports unchanged.

scenes.title: Every edit runs twice
scenes.sub: Once on your screen, once on the server
scenes.say: Chapter three. Every edit runs twice.

scenes.title: One agent edit, start to finish

steps.say: The agent does not get a hundred tools. It gets nine, and writes a short script with the kit's functions.
steps.term: MCP: how an agent calls tools

steps.say: Running it is a preview that saves nothing. A person looks, and approves.
The server runs the same command again on the newest model, with its own code. It never trusts the client's result.
If nobody else changed what it writes, it commits. If someone did, it refuses, and says who changed which field.
Say an agent builds a command on an older revision: set the height of one wall.
Meanwhile Priya, in another session, already changed that wall's height.

steps.term: Session: one browser tab or agent run
steps.say: The server re-runs the agent's command, finds she wrote the same field with another value, and refuses: Priya changed this wall's height while you were editing.
Had she changed the thickness instead, the agent's edit would simply commit, rebased onto her change.

scenes.title: Scans, renders and claims
scenes.sub: What the other tools do with capture data
scenes.say: Chapter four. Scans, renders and claims.

scenes.title: Pascal: a scene graph over a scan

steps.say: Pascal Editor keeps a building as a tree: site, building, levels, then walls, windows and rooms.
It is the only editor here that lets an agent work beside a scan, as a reference layer, through tools like create room and add door.

scenes.label: the most a Pascal phone-capture mesh may hold
scenes.note: otherwise a scan is a mesh file you place by hand
scenes.say: But in the open editor a scan is a mesh file you place by hand, and a phone capture's mesh holds at most twenty thousand faces. Not a building-scale point cloud.

scenes.title: vork's million birds, and the comparison
scenes.note: Blender times are projections from eight frames
scenes.say: At the far end sits vork, an engine an agent writes as code. Its million birds render in about ninety seven seconds. The Blender times are projections from eight frames.

scenes.title: Where the claims fall short
scenes.say: Reading the code took some shine off the posts.

items.say: Mutiny's kernel still declares walls, beams and columns. What it drains, on a ratchet, is mechanical, electrical and plumbing vocabulary.
Tested at two hundred and fifty thousand elements means a performance gate with budgets. A hundred and fourteen of its three hundred and thirty five rows are still pending.

items.text: No tool reads a point cloud
items.say: And none of these tools turns a registered point cloud into building elements.

scenes.text: The tool with a real building model cannot see a scan; the one that sees a scan stops at a reference layer.
scenes.say: So the tool with a real building model cannot see a scan yet, and the one that sees a scan stops at a reference layer. The step between is still a person with a prompt.

recap: Trades as add-ons on one kernel
Scans still stop at the model step
scenes.say: To recap. Trades as add-ons on one kernel. Every edit re-run, and refused by name. Scans still stop at the model step.
